safety_line: Gopher tortoises and their burrows are protected by Florida law. Do not disturb, handle, or fill a burrow — a permit is required even for construction work nearby.
traits: Half-moon-shaped burrow entrance with a sandy apron in front
Stumpy, elephant-like back legs and shovel-shaped front feet
Grazes on grass and low plants by day, 9-11 inches shell length
Burrow shared by more than 350 other species

look_alikes.difference: Gopher tortoise burrows have a half-moon entrance and sandy apron; pocket gopher mounds are small volcano-shaped soil piles with no open entrance.
look_alikes.next_photo: A wide photo of the burrow or mound shape, plus the shell if the tortoise is visible.

copy.what_it_means: Its burrow shelters more than 350 other species — Florida’s original landlord, and a protected species you’re lucky to host. Mow around the burrow apron and enjoy the neighbor; disturbing the burrow requires an FWC permit.
copy.fact: Its burrow shelters 350+ other species — Florida’s original landlord, and a protected species you’re lucky to host.

tech_notes: Threatened species under Florida law; burrow disturbance within 25 ft requires an FWC permit. Never treat, fill, or disturb a burrow — refer to FWC gopher tortoise program if relocation is requested.
